scope: Kubernetes/Kata persistent-volume single-writer and Tier-2 stale-writer fencing

observed_problem.description: The canonical StatefulSet reference used ReadWriteOnce for both persistent claims. Kubernetes documents RWO as node-scoped and capable of allowing multiple Pods on the same node to access one writable volume. ClayVerse requires one central entity, single-writer canonical state, and fail-closed Tier-2 stale-writer behavior.
observed_problem.strongest_counterhypothesis: replicas=1 plus external Tier-2 orchestration might normally prevent overlapping writers; however replacement/deletion races are exactly the failure boundary being fenced, and Kubernetes explicitly recommends ReadWriteOncePod for production StatefulSet single-Pod access.

changes: both StatefulSet persistent claims changed from ReadWriteOnce to ReadWriteOncePod
deployment contract now rejects ordinary RWO as insufficient for the one-entity/single-writer Tier-2 contract
final acceptance must prove the admitted CSI stack enforces ReadWriteOncePod and rejects an overlapping stale/replacement Pod writer
manifest carries persistent_volume_writer_fence and the matching final-pass requirement
focused regression forbids reintroduction of ReadWriteOnce and binds the contract/manifest gates

supporting_probe.identity_note: The reconstruction did not byte-match the moving canonical template, so this probe is deliberately not promoted to exact-file execution evidence. The GitHub commits/blobs are canonical source evidence; exact-current full regression remains a separate gate.

go_unusual_experiment.reason: No shared immutable request/turn id is exposed to this worker; only minute-precision trigger timing is available, so the canonical atomic lease protocol fails closed.

next_discriminator: On an admitted CSI-backed Kubernetes/Kata target, prove ReadWriteOncePod support and attempt an overlapping stale/replacement Pod mount against each ClayVerse PVC; the second writable attachment must be denied, then repeat through the Tier-2 full-sandbox replacement path.
